causes.text: Hurricane Helene struck Florida's Big Bend as a Category 4 storm on September 26-27, 2024, causing severe flooding, widespread property damage and downed trees and power lines across the southeastern U.S. The hurricane inflicted billions of dollars in damages and left homeowners facing extensive repairs.

source_info.title: Hurricane Helene Makes Landfall in the Florida Big Bend (September 26-27, 2024)

effects.text: On November 12, 2024, Home Depot said hurricanes Helene and Milton spurred a surge in demand for generators, batteries, plywood and other materials. The retailer reported that hurricane-related spending added roughly $200 million to sales and turned October comparable sales positive, prompting the company to forecast a smaller decline in annual revenue.

source_info.title: Home Depot expects smaller drop in annual sales as hurricane rebuild boosts quarter

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Sep 26-27, 2024: Hurricane Helene impacts multiple Southeastern states, damaging homes, roofs, and infrastructure. Emergency needs for generators, tarps, plywood, and batteries surge immediately, followed by demand for rebuild materials. Insurance processing and FEMA support provide additional funding flow into the repair channel over subsequent weeks.

Nov 12, 2024: Home Depot reports storm-related lift in traffic and ticket in affected markets, citing rapid mobilization of supply. Category strength in emergency and structural repair offsets softness elsewhere, improving sales mix. Management updates the quarter's outlook to incorporate elevated rebuild activity.

The event-driven upswing supports revenue visibility and cushions macro variability in non-affected regions. Investors rotate toward beneficiaries of repair-and-rebuild cycles; the stock advances roughly 2.0%.

rationale: The hurricane created an immediate need for repair and preparation materials. Home Depot's strong presence in affected regions enabled it to capture significant spending, directly linking the storm to the sales bump and investor reaction.
counterfactual_analysis: Absent Hurricane Helene, there would have been no sudden spike in demand for generators and building supplies. Home Depot's October sales would likely have remained weak, and the company might have maintained its previous, more pessimistic outlook.

adversarial_confounders.text: Seasonal promotions, unseasonably warm weather or competitor shortages could also affect sales. Nevertheless, the timing and the explicit mention of hurricanes Helene and Milton as drivers in Home Depot's statement reinforce the causal relationship.

details.commentary: Major hurricanes cause widespread damage that immediately boosts demand for building materials, generators and repair supplies at retailers like Home Depot. The surge in storm related purchases lifts quarterly sales and can influence future inventory and preparedness plans, reinforcing a cycle in which extreme weather events repeatedly drive spikes in home improvement spending.
